requirement:
The coverage check MUST consider every explicitly declared function or method
with a body in the first-party Rust sources of
{cite}`requirements.references.rust_item_coverage`, including test functions,
test helpers, and default trait methods. Declarations without bodies MUST NOT
create execution-coverage obligations. Source discovery or parsing failures
MUST cause the check to fail rather than silently omit functions.

A function whose measurement cannot be established MUST be reported as not
measured rather than silently excluded. Functions excluded by the selected
build configuration require exception evidence under
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.check.exceptions`.
rationale:
The tests in `src/execution_coverage/check.rs` cover each obligation in `requirements.test-coverage.check.scope`.

- **Every function or method with a body, including test functions, helpers and default trait methods.**
  - `mod[tests]/fn[methods_tests_and_helpers_are_included_and_discovery_failures_are_reported]` checks that `impl[S]/fn[method]`, `mod[tests]/fn[case]` and `mod[tests]/fn[helper]` each appear as "zero execution" obligations.
  - `mod[tests]/fn[default_trait_bodies_and_cfg_exclusions_are_obligations_but_declarations_are_not]` checks that `#trait[T]/fn[body]` is an obligation.
  - `mod[tests]/fn[overlapping_nested_functions_and_closures_do_not_cover_the_parent]` checks nested functions and closures. A nested function's count must not cover the outer function, and the outer function's count must not cover the nested one. Both directions are asserted.
- **First-party sources, excluding the project-root `vendor` directory.** `mod[tests]/fn[post_suite_scope_excludes_root_vendor_but_includes_source_vendor]` creates `vendor/foreign.rs` and `src/vendor/first_party.rs`. It asserts that the report names the second file and does not list the first. The report prints per-file lines as `- {file}: ...`, so the negative `- vendor/foreign.rs` assertion matches the real output format.
- **Declarations without bodies create no obligation.**
  - The default-trait-bodies test asserts that `fn[declaration]` never appears in the report.
  - It also calls `inventory` directly on `struct S; trait T { fn declaration(); }`.
  - The unmeasured-files test uses the same kind of declaration, and the file still reports "no executable obligations — pass".
- **Discovery or parse failures fail the check.**
  - The unmeasured-files test writes malformed Rust (`fn malformed(`) and asserts `!result.passed` plus a "cannot parse rust source" message.
  - The methods test corrupts `.git/index` and asserts failure with "cannot discover reference sources".
- **Unmeasurable functions are reported as not measured.**
  - The unmeasured-files test asserts `code.rs: not measured — FAIL` and `#fn[missing]: not measured`.
  - The default-trait-bodies test asserts that the `#[cfg(any())]` function appears as `#fn[excluded]: not measured` and the check fails.
- **Build-configuration exclusions need exception evidence.** The cfg-excluded function above fails the check without an exception. Acceptance and invalidation of exceptions belong to `requirements.test-coverage.check.exceptions`, which is cited here and has its own tests such as the one for accepted file and function explanations. They are outside this subject.

I found no plausible requirement-violating behavior that these tests would accept.

text: :::{req} check.scope
The coverage check MUST consider every explicitly declared function or method
with a body in the first-party Rust sources of
{cite}`requirements.references.rust_item_coverage`, including test functions,
test helpers, and default trait methods. Declarations without bodies MUST NOT
create execution-coverage obligations. Source discovery or parsing failures
MUST cause the check to fail rather than silently omit functions.
A function whose measurement cannot be established MUST be reported as not
measured rather than silently excluded. Functions excluded by the selected
build configuration require exception evidence under
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.check.exceptions`.
:::{req} rust_item_coverage

During repository validation, Habeas MUST parse every first-party Rust source file: every `.rs` file among the sources reference discovery considers under {cite}`requirements.references.discovery`, except those under the project-root `vendor` directory. Each explicitly declared function or method, including trait methods and test helpers, and each struct, enum, and union is an item that can be covered. An item is covered when it has a valid `{impl}`, `{cite}`, or `{test}` reference to a defined requirement or named example, or a valid citation of the built-in `habeas:util` under {cite}`requirements.references.util`, in a Rust comment attached to it or within its body; or when its outline node, or an outline node containing it, is recorded with its current hash as an outline input of an evidence record, a citation review, or a site review. Outline inputs recorded from selected search snippets under {cite}`requirements.authoring.finish_search.inputs` MUST count alongside mandatory inputs and additional reads. Comments belong to items under {cite}`requirements.references.outline_comments`; a comment before a field, variant, or attribute inside an item belongs to that item. A named example MUST reference a requirement under {cite}`requirements.examples.definition`. A reference in a string literal, on an enclosing module or impl block, or only in an evidence input MUST NOT count for the items it encloses. Habeas MUST report a Rust parse failure instead of silently skipping the file. Only {cite}`requirements.references.coverage.tests` and {cite}`requirements.references.coverage.examples` make an uncovered item a validation error; other items without recent coverage are warned about under {cite}`requirements.references.coverage.report`.
:::{req} check.exceptions
An unmet file threshold or an unexecuted or not-measured function MAY satisfy
the coverage policy only
through current, accepted, independently assessed evidence explaining why its
coverage is incomplete. An exception MUST be attached to the source file or
function whose incomplete coverage it justifies. A file-threshold exception
MUST NOT automatically excuse untested functions.
An exception MUST NOT excuse another source item's incomplete coverage.
Changes to the source item, justification, or other inputs
of its citation review MUST invalidate the affected exception under
{cite}`requirements.references.citation_review`.
A source comment or unassessed justification alone MUST NOT count as accepted
exception evidence. Function and gap identities MUST remain portable between
equivalent local and CI checkouts rather than depend on checkout paths,
run identifiers, timestamps, or process identifiers.
